newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Byblos Bank to list shares within month.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Byblos Bank to list shares within month.

text.p: Lebanon's Byblos Bank plans to list about 30 percent of its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange within a month, a bank executive said on Monday.
"About 30 percent of the shares will be listed on the Beirut Stock Exchange in the next month," Gerard Charvet, deputy general manager at Byblos, told Reuters.
"We will soon have a board meeting on the matter. We are in the final discussions with the central bank on how to proceed," Charvet added.

Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce last month became the first Lebanese bank to list its shares since the Beirut market reopened a year ago after a 13-year shutdown. The shares have risen daily since trading began on December 30.
Banque Audi, another leading Beirut bank, is also expected to list its shares shortly.

Lebanese banks are allowed under a 1995 law to list up to 30 percent of their shares on the exchange and trade is permitted without central bank permission except for transactions that raise an investor's stake to more than five percent of a bank's equity.
